title: cross-host-kv-lease-flap-diagnostic-log
content:
Summary:

Short incident note capturing a cross-host KV lease flapping event observed 2025-01-17 that precipitated eviction churn, high memory variance across hosts, and transient continuous-batching stalls. This doc records timeline, signals, hypotheses, commands used during triage, temporary mitigations applied, and proposed durable runbook entries. Aim: codify the investigative steps so future oncall can triage faster and avoid blind mitigation.

Scope and impact:
- Affected service: serving-runtime kv-cache allocator + batching coordinator (multi-tenant hosts in cluster-west).
- Customer impact: intermittent increased latencies for a subset of low-latency routes and a handful of request rate failures (5xx) for ~8 minutes during peak. No data loss.
- Observed host-level behavior: rapid lease reacquisition attempts for KV partitions spanning hosts A,B,C leading to repeated cache invalidation and spillback. Host memory spiked on hosts that lost leases and thrash-evicted large segments.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2025-01-17 10:02 UTC: first alert — memory deviation metric (host.mem.rss.p95) crossed 80% threshold on host-12 and host-17.
- 10:03 UTC: SRE alert noise escalated as batching SLO latency for route /stream-token generation exceeded 250ms.
- 10:05 UTC: automated eviction controller started churn (evict->prefetch->recover loop).
- 10:07 UTC: oncall paged; initial triage indicated cross-host lease reassignments in KV controller logs.
- 10:09 UTC: observed >200 lease-transfer events in 60s window for the same kv namespace (ns=robin-cache-v2).
- 10:12 UTC: temporary mitigation applied: raised lease-stabilization backoff and disabled aggressive prefetch for the namespace.
- 10:20 UTC: system recovered to baseline. Full postmortem TBD.

Signals / data collected during triage:
- Logs:
  - kv-controller: "lease-transfer req_id=... from host-12 -> host-17 state=preemptive reason=host-heartbeat-miss"
  - eviction-coordinator: repeated "eviction scheduled for segment s=0x7f... reason=lease-lost"
  - batch-coordinator: "batch-hold due to insufficient active shards count"
- Metrics:
  - host.mem.rss.p95 spike at hosts with lost leases (+35% over baseline)
  - lease.transfer.rate spiked from ~0.2/s to 3.6/s for ns=robin-cache-v2
  - batch.latency.p99 increased from 120ms -> 420ms on affected hosts
- Traces:
  - Distributed trace shows repeated retry loops in the KV client waiting for lease confirmation, adding ~50ms per token on average during transient.

Hypotheses considered (ranked):
1) Heartbeat jitter causing the lease manager to believe hosts are unhealthy and triggering aggressive failovers. Supporting signals: correlated heartbeat.err_count spikes in host-17 metrics and lease-transfer logs.
2) Race between prefetch/eviction code paths and lease-transfer handling leading to double-evictions (segment evicted on old host while new host prefetches). Supporting signals: eviction logs show evict for same segment immediately after prefetch start on another host.
3) Underlying network blips between host racks causing short-lived partitioning and causing lease flaps. Partial support: minor packet drops reported by infra for rack-3 during the window, but not sustained.
4) Bug in lease TTL refresh where races allow multiple hosts to think they own a lease briefly. No direct evidence yet, needs deeper reproducible test.

Commands / artifacts used in triage (for future oncall):
- kubectl logs -n serving-runtime kv-controller-xxx --since=15m | grep "lease-transfer" --context=3
- grep -n "eviction scheduled" /var/log/eviction-coordinator.log | tail -n 200
- prometheus query: rate(kv_lease_transfers_total{namespace="robin-cache-v2"}[1m])
- host-level: sudo journalctl -u heartbeat-agent -o short-iso --since "2025-01-17 09:55" | grep ERROR
- pprof heap snapshot from host-12 taken at 10:08 UTC (artifact: s3://redwood-telemetry/kv-leases/host-12-1008.heap)

Temporary mitigations applied (what we did live):
- Increased lease-stabilization.backoff_ms from 200 -> 1200 for namespace robin-cache-v2 (via dynconfig) to reduce reactive transfers.
- Disabled speculative prefetching for robin-cache-v2 for 20m (to break the feedback loop).
- Throttled eviction coordinator to 40% of normal throughput on host-12 to avoid further OOM cascade while stabilization took effect.
- Communicated to product: brief SLO blip, teams advised to monitor sensitive customers.

Effect of mitigations:
- lease.transfer.rate dropped back to ~0.3/s within 90s of dynconfig change.
- host memory trended down to baseline over 6 minutes after throttling eviction coordinator.
- batch.latency.p99 returned to ~140ms by 10:22 UTC.

Root cause analysis (working):
- Likely multiple contributors: transient network packet loss in rack-3 amplified by conservative heartbeat timeout and an opportunistic race between lease loss handling and prefetch/eviction logic. This produced a positive feedback loop: lease-flap -> eviction -> prefetch attempts on new host -> resource pressure -> missed heartbeats -> more lease transfers.
- No single code-level bug yet isolated; telemetry points to tuning + race conditions.

Action items (short-term):
- Create JIRA SRE ticket to track full postmortem and action items (JIRA-SRE-8421).
- Add a guard in lease-transfer path: if transfers > N in M seconds for a single namespace, escalate to sticky mode (reject transfers for a cooldown) — implement as config toggle. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Harden heartbeat agent to be less sensitive to transient packet loss: increase jitter and add exponential backoff. Owner: Aditi. ETA: 1 week.
- Add more fine-grained telemetry around prefetch vs eviction sequences per segment id to distinguish race orders (low-cost logging). Owner: Evelyn. ETA: 1 week.
- Add automated alert that correlates lease.transfer.rate with host.mem.rss.p95 to surface these coupled failures earlier. Owner: eng-sre. ETA: 3 days.

Action items (long-term):
- Design a test harness that can simulate partial rack partition and validate lease stabilization heuristics. Owner: platform-engineering + eng-sre. ETA: milestone Q2.
- Revisit eviction strategy to consider lease-confirmation semaphore before evicting hot segments that are actively being prefetched by another host. Owner: serving-runtime team. ETA: Q2 feature cycle.

Runbook insertions (draft lines to add):
- If you see a sudden correlated spike in lease.transfer.rate and host.mem.rss.p95 across multiple hosts, do not immediately scale eviction throughput up. Instead:
  1) Check lease.transfer.rate and recent heartbeat.err_count for hosts involved.
  2) Apply lease-stabilization dynconfig (backoff 1-2s) for the namespace as an emergency throttle.
  3) Temporarily disable speculative prefetch for affected namespace.
  4) Throttle eviction coordinator to avoid OOM cascade.
  5) If transfers continue >10/s for >3m, escalate to SRE lead and consider rolling restart of heartbeat-agent on implicated hosts.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we reproduce the race locally with a unit/integration test? (serving-runtime team to attempt)
- Is there a kernel-level NIC firmware issue showing up in infra packet loss logs? (infra to validate)
- Do tenants with high segment-churn have different failure modes? Run tenant-level analytics.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally written as a short-running oncall diary + immediate remediations. The full postmortem will expand with graphs and exact host IDs once offline analysis completes.
- Suggested reviewers: eng-sre leads, serving-runtime owners (kv, eviction, batching), platform infra networking.
summary: Cross-host KV lease flapping on 2025-01-17 caused eviction churn and batching latency regressions. Temporary mitigations (lease backoff, disable prefetch, throttle evict) stabilized system. Root cause likely interplay of heartbeat jitter, network blips, and a race between eviction and prefetch. Action items created for telemetry, config guard, and test harness.
